relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-node-to-node-encryption
relations.evidence: This command allows the enabling and disabling of node-to-node encryption this means data transferred between nodes in a cluster will be encrypted.

notable_absence.finding: This page states no precondition or incompatibility for toggling node-to-node encryption at all - it describes the operation as if it were a simple, always-available switch ('The command will execute a series of instructions in each node in the cluster to switch them from sending and receiving over a non-encrypted connection to an encrypted one or vice-versa'). But the already-promoted server:auto-failover concept states elsewhere in the corpus that auto-failover 'Must be disabled before an address-family change or a node-to-node-encryption change.' This page - the dedicated reference for making exactly that change - never mentions auto-failover, never tells the operator to disable it first, and gives no warning about what happens if it is left enabled. A genuine, checkable gap between what this CLI reference tells an operator and what the corpus elsewhere requires for the same operation to succeed safely.

cross_component_finding: This command's flag shape (--get/--enable/--disable, three mutually exclusive boolean switches) differs from its own explicitly cross-referenced sibling ip-family.md's shape (--get/--set plus separate --ipv4/--ipv4only/--ipv6/--ipv6only value flags) for what is, per server:cluster-address-family's own registry note, a tightly coupled pair of settings (an address-family change requires node-to-node encryption to be disabled first, and vice versa). Neither page explains the flag-shape asymmetry between the two commands it names as its own closest sibling.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none - node-to-node encryption is a self-managed Server cluster-topology setting with no Capella analog stated or implied on this page.
